Belarusian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • mama — Łacinka (Belarusian Latin alphabet)

Etymology

[edit]

A nursery word. From Proto-Slavic *mama, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *mā́ˀmāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂-méh₂, a reduplication of *meh₂- - the root of *méh₂tēr (“mother”). Cognate with German Muhme (“aunt”), Latin mamma (“mother, nurse”), Irish mam (“mother”), Lithuanian mama, moma (“mother”) among others. Cf. Proto-Slavic *tata, *baba.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈmama]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

ма́ма • (máma) f pers (genitive ма́мы, nominative plural ма́мы, genitive plural мам)

  1. mum / mom

Bulgarian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈmamɐ]
  • Syllabification(key): ма‧ма
  • Audio:(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

A nursery word, inherited from Proto-Slavic *mama.

Noun

[edit]

ма́ма • (máma) f

  1. mama, mom/mommy, mum/mummy
  2. (dialectal, by extension) mother's bosom, mammae
    Synonyms: бо́зка (bózka), (in animals) ви́ме (víme)

A nursery word. From Proto-Slavic *mama, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂-méh₂, a reduplication of *meh₂- - the root of *méh₂tēr (“mother”). Cognate with German Muhme (“aunt”), Latin mamma (“mother, nurse”), Irish mam (“mother”), Lithuanian mama, moma (“mother”) among others. Cf. Proto-Slavic *tata, *baba.

Old Ruthenian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic *ма́ма (*máma), from Proto-Slavic *màma, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *mā́ˀmāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂-méh₂, from *meh₂-, from *méh₂tēr (“mother”).[1][2][3] Cognate with Russian ма́ма (máma).

Noun

[edit]

мама • (mama) f

  1. mama, mummy, mommy, mum, mom (mother)

Related terms

[edit]
  • ма́мка f (mámka)

Descendants

[edit]
  • Belarusian: ма́ма (máma)
  • Carpathian Rusyn: ма́ма (máma)
  • Ukrainian: ма́ма (máma)

  2. ^ Melnychuk, O. S., editor (1989), “мама”, in Етимологічний словник української мови [Etymological Dictionary of the Ukrainian Language] (in Ukrainian), volume 3 (Кора – М), Kyiv: Naukova Dumka, →ISBN, page 375
  3. ^ Martynaŭ, V. U., editor (1990), “ма́ма”, in Этымалагічны слоўнік беларускай мовы [Etymological Dictionary of the Belarusian Language] (in Belarusian), volumes 6 (лі́ра – мая́чыць), Minsk: Navuka i technika, page 208

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak mama, from Proto-Slavic *mama. Cognates include Carpathian Rusyn ма́ма (máma) and Slovak mama.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈmama]
  • Rhymes: -ama
  • Hyphenation: ма‧ма

Noun

[edit]

мама (mama) f (diminutive мамка or мамочка, possessive adjective мамов)

  1. (childish) mom, mum, mommy, mummy
    Coordinate term: тато (tato)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of мама (mama)

nominative мама (mama) мами (mami)
genitive мами (mami) мамох (mamox)
dative мами (mami) мамом (mamom)
accusative маму (mamu) мами (mami)
instrumental маму (mamu) мамами (mamami)
locative мами (mami) мамох (mamox)
vocative мамо (mamo) мами (mami)

Related terms

[edit]
nouns
  • матка f (matka)
  • мац f (mac)

  • Medʹeši, H.; Fejsa, M.; Timko-Djitko, O. (2010), “мама”, in Ramač, Ju., editor, Руско-сербски словнїк [Rusyn-Serbian Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy

Russian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

A nursery word. From Proto-Slavic *mama, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *mā́ˀmāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂-méh₂, a reduplication of *meh₂- - the root of *méh₂tēr (“mother”). Cognate with German Muhme (“aunt”), Latin mamma (“mother, nurse”), Irish mam (“mother”), Lithuanian mama, moma (“mother”) among others. Cf. Proto-Slavic *tata, *baba.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈmamə]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Noun

[edit]

ма́ма • (máma) f anim or f inan (genitive ма́мы, nominative plural ма́мы, genitive plural мам, possessive adjective ма́мин, diminutive ма́мочка or ма́менька)

  1. mama, mummy, mommy, mum, mom (mother)
    Я Том, а э́то моя́ ма́ма. ― Ja Tom, a éto mojá máma. ― I am Tom and this is my mom.
  2. (computing slang) motherboard
  3. (figuratively) female socket

Etymology

[edit]

A nursery word. From Proto-Slavic *mama, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂-méh₂, a reduplication of *meh₂- - the root of *méh₂tēr (“mother”). Cognate with German Muhme (“aunt”), Latin mamma (“mother, nurse”), Irish mam (“mother”), Lithuanian mama, moma (“mother”) among others. Cf. Proto-Slavic *tata, *baba.
